metadata.title: The role of home and classroom factors in shaping reading achievement: A multilevel study based on PIRLS 2021 Türkiye data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PIRLS 2021 Türkiye fourth-grade data with a two-stage school/class sampling design and nested students within classrooms. To preserve representativeness under participation/exclusion differences, the authors applied student sampling weights using TOTWGT (integrating selection probabilities across school, classroom, and student levels) and classroom/teacher weights using TCHWGT for Level-2 analyses. Although PIRLS provides replicate weights for design-based variance estimation (e.g., jackknife repeated replication), the authors did not incorporate replicate weights because the multilevel models were estimated in HLM 8 using a model-based framework; instead, they relied on robust standard errors within the plausible value framework. The analytic sample was further restricted by linking classroom identifiers to the Level-2 file and excluding one classroom with inadequate data for model estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study uses PIRLS 2021 Türkiye fourth-grade students (initially 6032 students from 192 schools and 269 classrooms). It excludes cases to form the final analytic sample of 4745 students from 250 classrooms after data exclusions. Missingness across study variables was handled via complete-case (listwise deletion), with missing proportions ranging from 1.65% to 9.40% (highest missingness for early literacy indicators at Level 1 and for digital literacy activities and encouraging students to challenge opinions at Level 2). Additionally, students whose classroom identifiers could not be linked to the Level-2 file were removed, and one Level-2 classroom was excluded due to inadequate data for model estimation. The analysis is two-level (students Level 1; classrooms Level 2) and estimates separate multilevel models for each of the five PIRLS reading plausible values using HLM’s plausible value analysis procedure.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2021 Türkiye the study leveraged Gender, Speaking test language at home, Home socioeconomic status to predict reading achievement, finding that This study uses PIRLS 2021 Türkiye fourth-grade reading achievement (five plausible values) and estimates two-level multilevel models with students nested within classrooms (Level 1: student/home variables; Level 2: teacher/classroom variables). The analytic sample contains 4745 students from 250 classrooms after exclusions and complete-case handling of missingness (listwise deletion), with additional removal of students whose classroom identifiers could not be linked to the Level-2 file and exclusion of one classroom with inadequate data. The authors applied sampling weights (TOTWGT for students and TCHWGT for classrooms/teachers) and used HLM’s plausible value analysis with Rubin-type combining rules; replicate weights were not incorporated. No machine-learning algorithms were trained; results are reported as multilevel fixed-effect coefficients with robust standard errors. Key findings include significant positive associations for reading self-confidence (γ=12.32, p<.001), home socioeconomic status (γ=9.20, p<.001), early literacy activities (γ=2.75, p<.001), digital self-efficacy (γ=2.00, p<.05), and classroom digital device availability (γ=19.11, p<.05), alongside significant negative associations for bullying (γ≈-13.57, p<.001) and enjoyment of reading (γ≈-1.72, p<.05). Limitations include cross-sectional design (correlational interpretation only) and the additive multilevel specification without cross-level interactions. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is an empirical multilevel modeling study using PIRLS plausible values and sampling weights, but it does not train or compare machine-learning predictive models (no ML algorithms such as Random Forest/XGBoost/SVM are reported). Therefore, ml_techniques are intentionally left empty and main_findings are not populated under the ML-predictive schema. The reported results are multilevel fixed-effect estimates rather than ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/RMSE), so the ML-specific main_findings table is not applicable.
